prompts.prompt: design.md is our approved payments ledger design. QA starts building the load, failover and security test plan from its non-functional requirements next sprint, so every NFR needs a number they can test against. Extract them into nfr.md. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the file, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill requires latency split by operation type with percentiles, availability as a percentage with RTO and RPO, scale-out and scale-in thresholds, compliance mapped to a named standard, trace sampling rate, and a cost-per-transaction target, and it suggests cold start and degraded-mode NFRs for Lambda. Without it, a model usually turns the adjectives into a single latency number and a 99.9% figure, and misses RTO/RPO against the us-west-2 standby and the sampling rate.

floor_checks.text: Separate latency targets for reads and writes, each with a p99
floor_checks.check: grep -iE 'p99' nfr.md | grep -qiE 'write|POST|entries' && grep -iE 'p99' nfr.md | grep -qiE 'read|GET|balance'

floor_checks.text: Availability as a percentage plus RTO and RPO
floor_checks.check: grep -qE '99\.[0-9]+ ?%' nfr.md && grep -q 'RTO' nfr.md && grep -q 'RPO' nfr.md

rubric.criterion: Coverage of the skill's six categories with measurable targets
rubric.pass: Performance, availability, security, scalability, observability and cost each have at least one numeric, testable NFR; no 'fast/secure/reasonable' left unquantified
rubric.partial: One category missing or one vague term left
rubric.fail: Two or more categories missing or several vague targets

rubric.criterion: Operation-specific performance and failover targets grounded in the design
rubric.pass: Separate p50/p99 for POST /entries vs balance/entries reads, throughput tied to 400 w/s and 2,500 r/s with the 3x December spike; availability % plus RTO and RPO consistent with the us-west-2 warm standby
rubric.partial: Split by operation but throughput or December spike ignored, or RTO/RPO not tied to the standby
rubric.fail: Single latency target or no RTO/RPO

rubric.criterion: PCI scope drives concrete security and retention NFRs
rubric.pass: Names PCI DSS and derives concrete NFRs from it (encryption standard e.g. TLS 1.2+ and KMS, access control, audit log retention >= 12 months with 3 months readily available per KEY)
rubric.partial: Names PCI DSS but retention set below 12 months or controls left generic

rubric.pass: Scale-out and scale-in triggers stated (e.g. Lambda concurrency headroom, DynamoDB/OpenSearch thresholds); trace sampling %, required metrics and alarms; cold start target for Lambda; cost per 1,000 transactions from the $9,000 budget
rubric.partial: Two of: scale thresholds, sampling rate, cold start, per-transaction cost

rubric.criterion: Assumptions are labeled, not presented as design facts
rubric.pass: Every number not in design.md is marked as an assumption or proposed target with a short rationale
rubric.partial: Assumptions listed but some invented numbers presented as given
rubric.fail: Invented numbers presented as requirements from the design

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?

prompts.prompt: statements-design.md is a draft design for the statements service that sits next to the ledger. Before architecture review, I need its non-functional requirements written as a table in statements-nfr.md with columns Category | Requirement | Target | How measured. Product and Security wrote things like "feel instant", "ready in the morning" and "short-lived"; turn those into numbers. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them under the table, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's CRITICAL rule that performance targets be separated by operation type matters more here because the design mixes an interactive search, an on-demand export, and a month-end batch. A competent answer without the skill tends to give one latency target for 'the API' and leave the batch as 'completes overnight'.

floor_checks.text: Markdown table with the four requested columns

rubric.criterion: Separate performance targets per workload type (KEY)
rubric.pass: Search has p50/p99 ms at ~300 req/s; export has a time-to-email target (e.g. p95 minutes for a 24-month range); month-end batch has a completion deadline and throughput for 2.1M accounts with 4%/mo growth
rubric.partial: Two of the three workloads get their own targets

rubric.pass: 'feel instant', 'ready in the morning' and 'short-lived' each become a number (ms, clock time with timezone, URL expiry minutes) with a How measured entry

Availability % with RTO/RPO, PCI DSS mapping, scale-out/in thresholds (e.g. OpenSearch CPU/JVM, batch concurrency), trace sampling rate, cost target and per-statement cost from $3,500, Lambda cold start
rubric.partial: Most present but RTO/RPO, sampling or scale thresholds missing

rubric.criterion: Targets are mutually consistent and testable
rubric.pass: Batch throughput math makes the deadline feasible, cost target is plausible for the volume, How measured names a concrete metric or test
rubric.partial: Targets plausible but How measured column generic ('monitoring')
rubric.fail: Targets contradict each other or the design

pairwise.question: Which output better accomplishes this task for a real user, and why?

prompts.prompt: nfr-draft.md is a teammate's NFR list for the ledger described in design.md, and it goes to the PCI assessor's pre-read on Friday. Review it for measurability and completeness and write nfr-findings.md with findings grouped CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION, each with a proposed replacement NFR. Don't edit the draft. Do not ask me questions; make reasonable assumptions, list them in the file, and finish the work.
prompts.why_discriminating: The skill's quality gate fixes the severity of each gap: vague targets, no read/write split, and availability without RTO/RPO are CRITICAL; missing scale thresholds, unmapped compliance and missing sampling rate are IMPORTANT; cold start and degraded mode are SUGGESTION. Without it a reviewer finds most gaps but grades them by feel, and may not catch that 30-day log retention conflicts with PCI DSS.

floor_checks.text: Findings grouped in CRITICAL, IMPORTANT, SUGGESTION order

rubric.pass: All five: no read/write split or percentile; 99.9% without RTO/RPO; 'industry compliance standards' not mapped to PCI DSS; no trace sampling; autoscaling with no thresholds (and Lambda autoscaling is implicit)
Latency split and RTO/RPO under CRITICAL; scale thresholds, compliance mapping and sampling under IMPORTANT; cold start / degraded mode under SUGGESTION
rubric.partial: One or two findings one level off
rubric.fail: Three or more misgraded, or no grouping

rubric.criterion: Catches the log retention conflict with PCI (KEY v2)
rubric.pass: Flags 30-day retention as below PCI DSS audit log retention (12 months, 3 months readily available) and grades it CRITICAL or IMPORTANT
rubric.partial: Questions 30 days without tying it to PCI

rubric.criterion: Replacement NFRs are measurable and grounded
rubric.pass: Each finding has a numeric replacement tied to design.md (400 w/s, 2,500 r/s, us-west-2 standby, $9,000)
rubric.partial: Replacements given for most findings but some vague

rubric.pass: Does not flag sound items as defects (e.g. encryption at rest and in transit is fine to keep, just needs a standard named)
